notes.title: DNC/RNC National Committee Update
notes.content:
New Feature Update 
The National Committee System is a sophisticated political governance feature that simulates real life party committees where each major political party has a 50-member National Committee composed of one State Chair per state.

Core Features

Committee Structure

50 members total - One representative per state (State Chair)

Automatic membership - State chairs automatically become committee members

Weighted voting system - Voting power based on state party strength and ideological alignment


 Democratic Governance

Censure actions - Formal reprimands with 72-hour voting periods

Expulsion actions - Remove members from party with 168-hour voting periods (subject to change)

Revocation system - Remove censure status or readmit expelled members

Quorum requirements - 60% of total voting power must participate

Majority rule - Actions require 2/3 majority of votes cast to pass


Advanced Voting Mechanics

Weighted voting power = 1.0 × \[State Party Strength] / 100

Ideological alignment bonus - States more aligned with party stances get increased influence

Real-time vote tracking with detailed analytics and participation metrics


Subcommittee System

Campaign committees - DCCC, DSCC, DGA (Democratic) and NRCC, NRSC, RGA (Republican)

Treasury management - Each subcommittee starts with $1M and manages campaign funds

Leadership oversight - Committee can remove underperforming subcommittee chairs/members


Notification & Communication

Real-time alerts for all committee members on new proposals

Detailed action tracking with reasons, timestamps, and voting history

Comprehensive audit trail for all committee decisions

Strategic Depth
Leadership dynamics - Party leadership can manage committee composition and oversight

Performance accountability - Subcommittee leaders can be removed for poor performance

Gameplay Impact
Party discipline - Committees can enforce party loyalty and standards

Political consequences - Censured/expelled members face reputation penalties and restrictions

Campaign coordination - Subcommittees manage resources for electoral success

Democratic simulation - Realistic representation of how political parties actually govern themselves

notes.title: Supreme Court & Circuit Court Update
notes.content:
New Feature Update 


State bills can be challenged and sent to the Scotus.

Challenging a state bill costs 125 PC for members of that state, only members of a state can challenge bills in their own state.

Scotus members can challenge state bills in all states for 100 PC.

Circuit Court Judges can challenge state bills within their state jurisdiction for 75 PC, the cheapest.

Challenging a bill means that when it passes it must go to the SCOTUS

Furthermore, national bills NO LONGER automatically go to the Scotus. They must be challenged. 


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/07878b80b27206871f62f375dd94a36993f9c5cd.png"]

SCOTUS: 

100 PC to challenge any national bill Circuit Courts: 

125 PC to challenge any national bill Congress Members: 

150 PC to challenge any national bill Everyone else: 175 PC to challenge any national bill

notes.title: State Legislatures Alpha Update
notes.content:
New Feature Update

Rolled out Alpha State Legislatures

There is only 1 bill to gerrymander a state for a party, more to come, and be expanded later.

Governors can propose this bill in states without legs

Challenging a state bill costs 125 PC for members of that state, only members of a state can challenge bills in their own state. Challenging a bill means that when it passes it must go to the SCOTUS. 

Scotus members can challenge state bills in all states for 100 PC.

Circuit Court Judges can challenge state bills within their state jurisdiction for 75 PC.

Governors may veto state bills for 50 PC cost, delaying them by 12 hours and making them need 67% to pass.

States with state senates must have a bill go through the state house, then state senate before it has passed the legislature.

Circuit court members, members of states, and soctus members will need to look at legislatures if they want to try and block things. There should be notification for governors, state legislators/senators/etc for when a bill is active in their state.

notes.title: Presidential Interest Group System Update
notes.content:
New Feature Update


Candidates start at 13 IGP (Interest Group Points), Candidates get 1 an hour every hour for 48 hour Presidential Election, so in reality 60 total effective points.

Takes 80 points for all interest groups. You can feasibly fill out 6 full interest groups by the end of the Presidential Election.

An interest group being filled out is equivalent to 2 Target Ads in that interest group's states.

notes.title: Battle For The Hill - New Desktop App Release
notes.content:
What's New?


We're excited to announce the launch of our new desktop application for Battle For The Hill! This major update replaces the deprecated web-based version with a modern, native experience.


Native Desktop App - No more browser dependencies
 Improved Performance - Faster loading and smoother gameplay
 Better User Experience - Native dialogs and system integration
Auto-Updates - Automatic updates when new versions are available


Technical Improvements:


 Built with Electron for cross-platform compatibility
 Native file system access for better performance
 Integrated Steam Workshop support
 Enhanced error handling and recovery
 Improved memory management


Installation:

The new desktop app will automatically replace the old version. Your save data and settings will be preserved.

 Known Issues:

• First launch may take slightly longer as the app initializes
• Some users may need to restart Steam if the app doesn't launch immediately

Thank you for your patience during this transition! The new desktop app provides a much better gaming experience and sets the foundation for future updates.

notes.title: 🛠️ Scheduled Downtime Incoming: Major Update in Progress Development
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/8072d3788666eec2e024aa11709ac845690b5eb7.png

We wanted to give you a quick heads-up — Battle for the Hill will experience temporary downtime soon as we prepare to roll out our next major update. This update brings some of the biggest systems yet, and we’re excited to share what’s coming.

⚙️ What’s Being Worked On:

📊 New Stats System — Dynamic metrics that evolve with policy and gameplay choices.

💰 State Budget System — Functioning state-level budgets tied to gameplay, taxation, and public services.

🏛️ State Legislatures (SLs) — Interactive legislatures with real influence over lawmaking and budgets.

🏢 Corporate PvP Mechanics — A new layer of competitive gameplay between corporations and factions.

These new systems are foundational to expanding both game depth and strategic complexity, and we're hard at work making sure everything integrates smoothly.

🔧 Expected Downtime

The exact timing will be announced in the development discord linked on the steam. However, for your immediate information it will be on a infamous Friday.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/8072d3788666eec2e024aa11709ac845690b5eb7.png, but expect a short maintenance window.

We'll post again when a final schedule is locked in, along with full patch notes.

Thanks for your patience and support as we take Battle for the Hill to the next level. More updates soon — stay tuned!

— The BFTH Team

notes.title: Iteration 14 North America Federation (Complete Reset) Is here on January 11th!
notes.content:
Iteration 14 (Complete Reset) Is here

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/71c03287e249f19684d1dbf3018d13d8177d7f64.png

This coming iteration of BFTH will feature two parties included with Independents, and a special surprise in content thanks to our newest sponsors. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/846b0ce70157fae591df4fea1ae143a0883133de.png

We are thrilled to unveil Iteration 14, the most ambitious update yet for Battle for the Hill (BFTH), introducing a geopolitical twist, the North American Federation. In this latest iteration, Canada and the United States have united under one cohesive political system, transforming Canada’s provinces into fully fledged states. This monumental shift stems from real-world events.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/91e199d4673dbd8d5fb6e16e164253e3e524a89f.png

The integration of Canadian provinces has reshaped the legislative landscape. The Senate now boasts 120 seats, reflecting the inclusion of representatives from the new states. The House of Representatives expands to 495 seats, accommodating the increased population and ensuring proportional representation.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44949145/f9f12a1796f02aeb0322be3769cf368ca9e25bd4.png

The electoral vote count has been adjusted to 618, with the magic number to win the presidency set at 310. This recalibration adds layers of strategy, as players must now navigate a newer intricate and competitive electoral map. With new states in the mix players will need to adapt to this larger, more dynamic playing field. 270 to win doesn't seem so bad now huh

Canadian states bring unique cultural, economic, and political challenges to the game. Enjoy exploring their economic system, and their provincial economies.

The fate of the North American Federation lies in your hands. Will you unite the people under a common vision, or will the challenges of integration prove too great? 

Step into Iteration 14 and find out in Battle for the Hill.
